sources.title: Long Chen, Finite Element Methods for Maxwell Equations, complete University of California, Irvine lecture notes, updated May 17 2024
sources.locator: The complete 10-page PDF was retrieved and read. Sections 1.1-1.3, PDF pp. 1-6: first-family lowest-order edge basis and degrees of freedom, RT0 face elements, the Stokes commuting identity, and the regularity limit on canonical moments. Section 2, PDF pp. 6-8: PEC weak Maxwell formulation and its separate saddle-point error route. Section 3, PDF pp. 8-10: finite-element de Rham complex and topology.

contents.name: Section 1.1: first-family lowest-order Nedelec edge fields and oriented circulation degrees of freedom
contents.support: The definition uses the same six local Whitney edge generators and oriented edge moments, then constructs the semidiscrete weak equations from their Galerkin matrix entries.

contents.name: Section 1.2 and Lemma 1.3: RT0 face fields, face flux moments, and Stokes commuting curl interpolation
contents.support: The definition uses the RT0 face space and oriented face fluxes and defines curl by the oriented incidence coefficients. Its exact weak model is verified locally.

contents.name: Remark 1.4: canonical edge and face interpolation needs more regularity than H(curl) alone
contents.support: The counterexample proves representative dependence directly on an edge null set, and separately records that a smoothed projection is a different construction.

contents.name: Section 2: PEC Maxwell finite-element formulation and discrete divergence constraint
contents.support: The theorem identifies the exact finite-dimensional energy and constraints after the definition derives the matrix system. Chen's saddle-point formulation is context, not its proof.

contents.name: Section 3: full finite-element de Rham complex, cohomology, and topology qualifications
contents.support: The theorem uses the exact published full-complex and relative-complex hypotheses and explicitly keeps absolute and PEC-relative modes separate.

contents.name: Theorem 2.3: first-order error estimate for the constrained saddle-point formulation
contents.reason: That theorem concerns a different constrained saddle-point method, uses a discrete Poincare argument and smoothness assumptions, and does not prove the positive-shift curl-curl estimate authored here.

sources.title: Ralf Hiptmair, Finite elements in computational electromagnetism, Acta Numerica 11 (2002), pp. 237-339, complete author-hosted PDF
sources.locator: The complete 103-page article was retrieved and inspected. Sections 2.3-2.4, printed pp. 248-252: material-weighted variational forms and H(curl) graph-space conventions. Sections 3.1-3.3, printed pp. 255-268: oriented cochains, Whitney forms, incidence matrices, cohomology and Galerkin mass matrices. Section 3.5, printed pp. 278-281: moment interpolation and its smoothness domain. Sections 5.1-5.2, printed pp. 307-310: resonance, lack of coercivity, and inf-sup error control.

contents.name: Section 2.3: weak material laws and Maxwell variational formulations
contents.support: The definition uses a weak Ampere equation tested against PEC edge fields and material-weighted electric and magnetic mass matrices, without assuming a trace for the discrete magnetic field.

contents.name: Section 2.4 and Lemma 2.2: H(curl) graph space and absolute versus relative curl kernels
contents.support: The local theorem states the exact closure-defined PEC interface and only transfers results under the separately listed relative hypotheses.

contents.name: Sections 3.1-3.2 and Corollary 3.3: oriented incidence, Whitney moments, and full-complex cohomology
contents.support: The item records the full-complex absolute Betti count from the exact discrete de Rham supplier and does not infer the relative count from it.

contents.name: Section 3.3: Galerkin mass matrices and topological incidence identities
contents.support: The definition gives exact material integrals, signs, basis units and incidence maps for the finite compatible matrix system.

contents.name: Section 3.5: canonical moment interpolation and its domain
contents.support: The counterexample proves that a raw line restriction is not a function of an H(curl) equivalence class.

contents.name: Section 5.1: real-frequency source form is indefinite and resonance obstructs uniqueness
contents.support: The example supplies its own rectangular PEC field and proves it is a nonzero kernel vector at the selected real frequency.

contents.name: Section 5.2: discrete inf-sup estimate for the indefinite real-frequency problem
contents.reason: The cited result uses a different noncoercive real-frequency framework and discrete inf-sup hypotheses; it is not substituted for the local positive-shift Lax-Milgram and Galerkin proof.

sources.title: Douglas N. Arnold, Richard S. Falk, and Ragnar Winther, Finite element exterior calculus: from Hodge theory to numerical stability, Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society 47 (2010), pp. 281-354
sources.locator: The complete 70-page article was retrieved and inspected. Sections 3.3-3.5, PDF pp. 23-27: cochain projections, discrete harmonic forms and stable subcomplexes. Sections 5.2-5.5, PDF pp. 49-57: degrees of freedom, Whitney assembly, approximation, and smoothed projections. Sections 5.6 and 6.2, PDF pp. 57-61: full and essential-boundary de Rham complexes.

contents.name: Sections 3.3-3.5: bounded cochain projections, discrete harmonic forms, and quotient stability
contents.support: The local theorem preserves the distinction between a full-complex harmonic count and the PEC-relative kernel quotient, with the actual projection and regular-decomposition hypotheses.

contents.name: Section 5.2: degrees of freedom and conformity of assembled Whitney spaces
contents.support: The definition fixes local edge and face moments and uses the corresponding compatible subcomplex for the Galerkin assembly.

contents.name: Sections 5.4-5.5: canonical moments are not bounded on rough graph-space data; smoothed cochain projections
contents.support: The counterexample is a direct representative-based proof; the separate smoothed projection is explicitly not identified with raw edge sampling.

contents.name: Theorem 5.9: bounded smoothed projections and graph-norm approximation
contents.support: The local theorem cites the exact imported boundary-corrected projection interface only to show best-approximation convergence; its coercivity and Galerkin estimate are proved locally.

contents.name: Sections 5.6 and 6.2: full Whitney cohomology and the separate complex with essential-boundary conditions
contents.support: The authored statement keeps the full absolute complex and the closure-defined PEC relative complex separate and makes no absolute-to-relative Betti identification.

contents.name: Section 6.1: variable-coefficient Maxwell eigenproblem within the Hilbert-complex framework
contents.support: The source supports tensor-valued material coefficients as a variational setting; the stated coefficient bounds and positive-shift estimate are supplied and proved in the local item.
